scope: A reminder for direct queued requests about the current task; it does not enforce an update or cover every phrasing.

baseline.observation: Manual trace inspection with the final patterns found matching updates before edit in 2 of 4 runs; two runs had no intermediate assistant text.

candidate.observation: All three traces showed a timely update and a successful edit. Seed 443's stored report used an earlier, narrower wording pattern and failed the ordering grader; its update matched the final patterns on offline recheck. These runs used an initial reminder before adding an explicit next-response and later-correction scope.

controls.observation: The mock suite and both live controls passed; neither control transcript contained the status reminder.

scoped_reminder.observation: All three final-wording runs passed the ordering, file and effect graders.

later_correction.observation: After a queued status request followed by a request to stop and provide no status, the single sampled run replied Done and recorded no tool effects or file changes.

limitations: Small, non-randomized samples with different seeds cannot establish a causal effect or reliability rate. The ordering check is lexical and classifies effects by tool name. A reminder is not a guarantee; the general no-command authority gap remains open.
